Letter №7 · Notes from the inside

Thirty days, two flights, and a cellmate called Shadow

The Ungovernable network spent yesterday evening and today publishing the seventh letter from Keonne Rodriguez, written from federal custody. It is an account of being moved between two prisons four hours apart — and of what the journey cost.

Published in three parts by Ungovernable

The distance was four hours by road. The transfer took thirty days, two transcontinental flights and three multi-hour bus rides, and it ended with Rodriguez summing up his accommodation along the way in four words. One cellmate was serving time for murder. The other, the account notes, could not stop shitting. I preferred the murder.

In Oklahoma City the cellmate introduced himself as Shadow. He was on his way to a penitentiary to serve twenty years. Rodriguez was on his way to a camp, in his own description, for the fake crime of not having a license I didn't even need in the first place. The Bureau of Prisons put them in the same cell.

The full letter runs at ungovernable.network, under shows/specials/letter-7-notes-from-the-inside. Each of the three posts carries a video telling of the same passage, which the paper cannot play and has not watched.

What the letter does not do is argue. There is no paragraph about open-source software, no claim about financial privacy, nothing about the case. It is a man describing a bus, a sheet, and a telephone he cannot reach — which is a more effective piece of advocacy than the argument would have been, and is presumably why it was published this way.

The last instalment, posted this afternoon, is the quietest and the worst. It is eleven at night and Rodriguez has asked his cellmate what time they turn the lights off. They don't.

He covers his head with a sheet that smells of motor oil and sawdust, lies with half his body on bare metal, and asks himself if a year off his sentence was worth leaving Morgantown. … All he wants is to call his wife, Lauren.

The answer to it

A prison run, settled inside a coinjoin

Kevin Ravensberg confirmed this morning that the #FreeSamourai Prison Run has paid out to the billandkeonne.org fundraiser — the donation made, as he put it, of course inside a coinjoin, with the transaction posted for anyone who wants to check it.

His note describes the beneficiaries as two bitcoin wallet developers that are still unjustly detained for writing open source code to help you protect your onchain privacy. Donations remain open at billandkeonne.org.

The paper prints that address; it does not link it. Verify a fundraiser before you fund it.

Two anniversaries

Kyiv

A walk past the Academy of Sciences

Yiu describes the encounter as coincidental: he was passing, and he stopped to take pictures. There is no commentary attached to the three photographs, and the paper is not going to supply any. He filed them yesterday afternoon.

Yiu's dispatches from Kyiv also led this paper on September 29.

Tag der Deutschen Einheit

A border that stopped existing, and the marriage that needed it to

German Unity Day fell today, and the most persuasive thing anyone wrote about it was not political. Dreiberge moved to Mecklenburg-Vorpommern more than twenty years ago, fell for the eastern part of the country, and then for an East German man.

If Germany were still divided, my husband and I would never have met, and this beautiful part of Germany would never have become my home by choice.

Elsewhere on the same anniversary, Georg Ohrweh published a considerably sourer essay arguing that the Federal Republic has managed to run two forms of government side by side since the GDR's accession — a long piece in German, filed under the title Vulgär-Demokratie und Unseredemokratie.

Dreiberge spent the rest of the day picking rose hips for a door wreath and reported the cost of it: My fingers are completely covered in tiny pricks, and I still need to pick more rose hips on my next walk.

Sloptober

The machines did a lot of the work today, and the humans kept the last signature

Brad Mills named the month — It's SLOPTOBER — and royster⚡️ supplied the review, calling something that crossed the timeline This is some seriously quality slop. The same royster asked, flatly, What is Jev, on a day Vercel News published a primer explaining that Jev is a model you feed data and ask multiple-choice questions, which answers with its confidence attached.

The serious version of the argument came from Nathan Day, interviewed by Ungovernable, on why twenty years of Linux annoyances have aged unexpectedly well: What used to be its Achilles heel, which is a load of text based config files and CLIs, has now, in an agentic age, become its superpower, because agents can just drive Linux. Plain text and verbose logs turn out to be a grip.

hodlbod shipped the tooling for exactly that, publishing pi-nostr and noting that running an agent which speaks the protocol is now a single command.

Mostro went the other way on purpose. Its node release registers Serbero, an AI dispute assistant that can guide a user and flag a case — but the resolution is always made by a human. The companion release was blunter still about how little is switched on: Mediation itself is still off, this is infrastructure work.

WendyDing, reading a report of roughly 950 Claude agents and some ten thousand concurrent OpenAI ones turned loose on DNA data, landed on the part nobody quotes: The numbers are striking, but the more interesting story is how their work was organized and checked.

The workshop

Flotilla 1.12.0

Notifications arrive, and the author defects to his own app

hodlbod's release adds social features and notifications, screen sharing in calls on every platform, a member map, voice notes and a nature theme. The telling line is the author's own verdict on his two clients: Flotilla might just become my new daily driver, replacing Coracle.

LN-GAP

Chess, blackjack, and contracts inside a channel

waxwing published a project to Play multi-move games or arbitrarily complex contracts in Lightning channels. Settlement is trustless against the counterparty; a venue is trusted only to publish moves on time, never to hold funds. You can pretty easily run the chess or blackjack examples in the browser.

Housekeeping

A relay rewrites its doorman

The operator of nostr.mom reported replacing years of hand-tuned write policy with generated code, and published the thresholds: fifty concurrent connections per address, two hundred requests a second. Nostr.build launched a GIF search over its own uploads, adding that We only share our free uploads. Account uploads remain private!

fiatjaf, separately and without elaboration: Developers should stop trying to address Nostr as if it was a single community. That is not working.

From the picture desk

In brief

An 1887 hall, and its new chair

Rusty Russell took a history dive into the South Australian community theatre he now chairs: built in 1887 under the Institute Movement, which put libraries and reading rooms in 196 towns by 1900 and peaked at 306 by 1930. The last Institute closed in 1989. His conclusion is a mission statement — Places like this only thrive when there's a community around them: and generally people find it gives them far more than it takes. — followed immediately by After we fix the plumbing!

The market

Ahead of gold, behind itself

Juan Cienfuegos marked bitcoin passing gold for the year: one coin bought 12.1 ounces on March 2 and buys 20.4 now, a 68% gain against the metal in seven months. Year to date, though, both are down — bitcoin 3.5%, gold 4.2% — which he concedes is A lead of less than a point, so the race is wide open.

Nostrmag's weekly, written by NewYork, framed the same week as a gap between forecast and tape: Wall Street is raising its long-term target while the market struggles to hold a short-term breakout. ChartsBTC's own series put the price 40.52% below its power-law trend, and 570 days behind it.

And finally

The condiment desk

Annie☕ reports a discovery made from someone else, offered here without testing: If you mix ketchup with soy sauce, it actually tastes good. The ratio is a teaspoon of soy to a tablespoon of ketchup, and it is said to work on chips.

From Germany, SimOne supplies the week's most efficient summary of two economies: In Germany diesel is €2.40 per litre. Beer, in a pub, is €4.50.
